readme:
# ACT 动作块时间集成与风格正则

## 1. 问题

实现对当前动作的重叠预测集成，以及条件VAE的标准正态KL。

实现ACT的两个张量核心；输入已经对齐到同一执行时刻，省略视觉Transformer、动作块网络和遥操作系统。

## 2. 核心公式

$$
\bar a=\frac{\sum_{i=0}^{K-1}e^{-ki}a_i}{\sum_i e^{-ki}},\quad L_{KL}=\frac1{2B}\sum_{b,d}(\mu_{bd}^2+e^{\ell_{bd}}-1-\ell_{bd}).
$$

## 3. 公式到代码

- `temporal_ensemble(actions: Tensor, valid: Tensor, decay: float) -> Tensor`
- `style_kl(mu: Tensor, logvar: Tensor) -> Tensor`

官方实现按旧到新索引使用负指数；因此正decay给较早预测更大权重。显式valid替代源码的全零哨兵，避免把合法零动作丢掉。KL中的logvar是对数方差。

## 4. 本题约定

actions为(K,D)，valid为(K,)布尔，至少一条有效；有效预测按生成时间从旧到新排列，先去padding再按0..Kvalid-1赋权，k>=0。mu/logvar为(B,Z)，KL按潜变量求和、按batch平均。保留浮点输入梯度。

校验辅助函数已提供。浮点输入为有限 CPU float32/float64，不修改输入；非法形状、类型、范围或掩码必须抛出 `ValueError`。

## 5. 交互图与确定性实验

对64个固定正弦目标构造五份交替误差预测，比较时间集成与最新单次预测的MSE；同时用KL梯度将风格均值移向零。

可视化由 `viz/gen.py` 生成；T3 将你的函数传入同一实验并记录真实指标。这是小规模确定性教学实验，不是机器人基准成绩。

## 6. 在网页中运行

在右侧 Python 编辑器中补全实现，点击 **运行测试**。查看失败测试的原因、期望值与实际值，修改代码后再次运行。所有必要测试通过后，题目会标记为已完成并解锁坑点讲解。

## 7. 来源与延伸

- [Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.13705) — Temporal ensembling at inference; official imitate_episodes.py exp_weights and CVAE policy KL
- [Verified source](https://github.com/tonyzhaozh/act/blob/main/imitate_episodes.py)
- [Verified source](https://tonyzhaozh.github.io/aloha/)

核验日期：2026-10-28。扩展到完整论文系统还需要本题范围中明确省略的模型、数据和环境。
notes:
# ACT: 题解与易错点

官方实现按旧到新索引使用负指数；因此正decay给较早预测更大权重。显式valid替代源码的全零哨兵，避免把合法零动作丢掉。KL中的logvar是对数方差。

padding不应占据指数序号；所有动作坐标共享一组时间权重。KL遗漏维度求和会让潜变量数改变正则强度。

## 测试捕获的错误

- Temporal weights favor newest predictions instead of the declared official ordering.
- KL incorrectly averages latent dimensions.

## 实验范围

实现ACT的两个张量核心；输入已经对齐到同一执行时刻，省略视觉Transformer、动作块网络和遥操作系统。

## 可重复实验记录

64个正弦目标、5个重叠预测，decay=0.01；基线为最新预测。另将4×3风格均值用40步梯度下降(lr=0.5)推向标准正态。要求集成MSE<最新预测10%，最终KL<初始1e-4。

判题固定seed=42。计算采用CPU float64、显式输入，涉及优化时使用普通梯度更新；不下载数据集或模型权重。原生PyTorch与真实Pyodide/NumPy-WASM执行同一套T0–T3测试。阈值针对本教学实验。

en.readme:
# ACT Temporal Action Ensembling and Style Regularization

## 1. Exercise goal

Ensemble overlapping predictions for the current action and compute the CVAE standard-normal KL.

Implement two ACT tensor cores with predictions already aligned to one execution time; omit the visual Transformer, action-chunk network and teleoperation system.

## 2. Core equations

$$
\bar a=\frac{\sum_{i=0}^{K-1}e^{-ki}a_i}{\sum_i e^{-ki}},\quad L_{KL}=\frac1{2B}\sum_{b,d}(\mu_{bd}^2+e^{\ell_{bd}}-1-\ell_{bd}).
$$

## 3. From equations to code

- `temporal_ensemble(actions: Tensor, valid: Tensor, decay: float) -> Tensor`
- `style_kl(mu: Tensor, logvar: Tensor) -> Tensor`

The official implementation applies a negative exponential to oldest-to-newest indices, favoring older predictions for positive decay. Explicit validity replaces its all-zero sentinel so zero actions remain valid. Logvar means log variance.

## 4. Contract and boundaries

Actions are (K,D), valid is bool (K,) with at least one true. Valid predictions are oldest-to-newest; remove padding then assign ranks 0..Kvalid-1, decay>=0. Mu/logvar are (B,Z); KL sums latent coordinates and averages examples. Preserve floating-input gradients.

Validation helpers are provided. All floating inputs are finite CPU float32/float64; do not mutate inputs. Invalid shape, dtype, range or mask arguments raise `ValueError`.

## 5. Deterministic experiment and visualization

Construct five alternating-error predictions of 64 sinusoidal targets and compare ensemble MSE with the latest prediction; also optimize a style mean toward zero using the submitted KL.

The visualization is generated by `viz/gen.py`; T3 runs the same experiment with your functions and records its actual metrics. These are small deterministic teaching results, not a robot benchmark.

## 6. Run your implementation

Complete the functions in the Python editor on the right, then click **Run tests**. Inspect each failed check, update your implementation, and run again. Passing every required check marks the problem as solved and unlocks the notes.

## 7. Sources and extensions

- [Learning Fine-Grained Bimanual Manipulation with Low-Cost Hardware](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.13705) — Temporal ensembling at inference; official imitate_episodes.py exp_weights and CVAE policy KL
- [Verified source](https://github.com/tonyzhaozh/act/blob/main/imitate_episodes.py)
- [Verified source](https://tonyzhaozh.github.io/aloha/)

Verified 2026-10-28. Extending this operator to the full paper requires the omitted model, data and environment described in the scope above.
en.notes:
# ACT: Solution notes

The official implementation applies a negative exponential to oldest-to-newest indices, favoring older predictions for positive decay. Explicit validity replaces its all-zero sentinel so zero actions remain valid. Logvar means log variance.

Padding must not consume exponential ranks, and all action coordinates share temporal weights. Averaging instead of summing latent dimensions changes KL strength with latent size.

## Mistakes caught by the tests

- Temporal weights favor newest predictions instead of the declared official ordering.
- KL incorrectly averages latent dimensions.

## Experimental scope

Implement two ACT tensor cores with predictions already aligned to one execution time; omit the visual Transformer, action-chunk network and teleoperation system.

## Reproducible protocol

64 sinusoidal targets, five overlapping predictions, decay .01; latest prediction is the baseline. Fit a 4×3 style mean toward a standard normal using 40 gradient steps at lr .5. Require ensemble MSE below 10% of latest-prediction MSE and final KL below 1e-4 of initial KL.

The judge fixes seed 42. All calculations use CPU float64, explicit inputs and plain gradient updates where applicable; no datasets or model weights are downloaded. Native PyTorch and actual Pyodide/NumPy-WASM run the same T0–T3 suite. Thresholds refer to this teaching adaptation.
